study_type.claude: Mixed methods (concurrent embedded design: survey, PLS-SEM, OLS, qualitative analysis)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (concurrent embedded design: survey, PLS-SEM, OLS, qualitative analysis)
study_type.note: Survey-based concurrent embedded design (quantitative modelling plus open-ended responses).

research_method.claude: Concurrent embedded mixed methods: survey with 5-point Likert items; EFA (JASP); PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4) for RQ1; OLS with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for RQ2; qualitative coding of open-ended answers (Jaccard IRR); 688 responses, 442 valid; G*Power minimum 119
research_method.nlm: Concurrent embedded mixed methods: survey (N=442), PLS-SEM, OLS regression with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, qualitative coding (IRR >= 90%), power analysis
research_method.value: Concurrent embedded mixed-methods survey grounded in the JD–R model; 5-point Likert constructs; EFA and PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4) for RQ1; OLS regression with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment for RQ2; qualitative coding of open-ended responses; 688 responses, 442 valid
research_method.note: EFA and the 688 raw responses reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry/Mixed; professional developers recruited from 56 OSS communities (organizational repositories of Microsoft, Google, Netflix, Red Hat, IBM; Kubernetes, Hugging Face, Python, TensorFlow) and professional groups; N = 442
context.nlm: Mixed (industry and OSS communities, incl. Microsoft, Google, Netflix, Red Hat, IBM repositories and Kubernetes, Hugging Face, TensorFlow); N = 442 professional developers
context.value: mixed; professional developers recruited via 56 OSS communities (organizational repositories such as Microsoft, Google, Netflix, Red Hat, IBM; Kubernetes, Hugging Face, Python, TensorFlow) and professional groups; 442 valid survey respondents
context.note: Claude writes 'Industry/Mixed'; treated as the same category as NotebookLM's 'Mixed'.

dora_applied.note: DORA 2024 report only cited in background (both).

space_applied.note: SPACE only cited via Houck et al. (both).

ai_discussed.note: GenAI adoption is the study's object (JD–R model of burnout).

remote_covid.note: Work mode not reported by either; COVID-19 appears only in the source of adapted workload items.

data_window.note: Not stated by either; full text says only that the survey was available for two weeks, without dates.

cat_productivity.note: Productivity not measured; NotebookLM lists task speed-up only from cited literature.

cat_quality.note: Code quality only from the cited DORA report (NotebookLM).

cat_collaboration.note: Borderline: no collaboration metric measured; both report the 'hidden collaboration costs' finding (review burden of AI output) and the recommendation that KPIs include review effort.

cat_satisfaction.note: Burnout construct (4 Likert items adapted from Trinkenreich et al.) is the dependent variable.

cat_activity.note: Claude tags self-reported AI-use frequency and NotebookLM tags perceived workload as Activity; neither is repository activity.

cat_delivery.note: Delivery performance only from cited literature (DORA 2024).

cat_devex.note: Both tag some JD–R constructs 'DevEx', but the DevEx framework is not used.

cat_survey.note: All constructs measured by 5-point Likert survey items.

evidence.quote: We employed a concurrent embedded mixedmethods research design, integrating quantitative and qualitative evidence. We first surveyed 442 developers across diverse organizations, roles, and levels of experience.
We first leveraged Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) [87] to analyze the survey data to evaluate hypotheses H1 to H3
We first used ordinary least squares (OLS) regression models [37] to assess the relationship between developer characteristics and job demands, resources, and burnout.
We received 688 responses. After excluding invalid responses, the final dataset comprised 442 participants.
we recruited software developers from 56 Open Source Software (OSS) communities spanning diverse domains, including organizational repositories (e.g., Microsoft, Google, Netflix, Red Hat, IBM)
We also reached out to data science-oriented communities (e.g., Python, TensorFlow) and professional groups.
In this paper, we investigate the relationship between the adoption of GenAI and developers' burnout.
The last survey section measured burnout through participants' perceptions through a set of 4 statements which participants rated on a 5-point Likert scale
We measured organizational pressure by asking participants to rate 4 statements on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree; N/A if not applicable).
Shift 3: From productivity gains to hidden collaboration costs.
improve workload equity by rotating reviewer responsibilities and updating KPIs to include these efforts.
